units.title: Y101 Alfred and the Making of England 871–1016

outcomes.text: Describe Alfred's weak position in 871 and the threat of the Great Heathen Army.
Explain Alfred's refuge at Athelney, the defeat of the Heathen Army, the peace terms and the capture of London in 886.
Assess why Alfred succeeded militarily: leadership, strategy, tactics, resources, army and navy reforms, logistics and chance.
Explain the return of the Vikings in the 890s.

subtopics.title: Alfred and the governance of England

outcomes.text: Describe Alfred's administrative reforms and how he built unity in his territory.

Assess the role of translations, Bede's History, Asser and Latin education for priests.
Explain how literature was used as propaganda.

subtopics.title: Absolute monarchy and the role of ministers

outcomes.text: Explain the theory of absolutism and the authority and rule of Louis XIII and Louis XIV.
Describe administration, centralisation, intendants and governors, Versailles as a symbol of absolutism and the king's legal position.
Describe finances, taxation and noble privileges, and assess Richelieu, Mazarin, Colbert and Le Tellier.
Explain the Most Christian King, relations with the French Church, Papacy, Jesuits and Catholic Orders.
Explain Gallicanism, Louis XIV's quarrels with Innocent XI and the regale.
Explain relations with the Huguenots: Peace of Alais, Dragonnades and the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes and its impact.
Explain the significance of Jansenism and royal reactions.
Describe the status and prosperity of nobility, clergy, merchants and peasants.
Explain noble and court unrest: Chalais, duelling, Day of Dupes, Cinq Mars and the Fronde.
Describe peasant rebellions (Va-Nu-Pieds, Croquants) and 1690s hardships and tax revolts.
Explain French foreign policy aims and France as a power 1610–1635, and the impact of the Thirty Years War.
Explain Louis XIV's wars against Spain, the United Provinces, England and the Empire and the treaties of Westphalia, Pyrenees and Utrecht.

topics.title: Depth Studies: The Ascendancy of France

subtopics.title: Richelieu's relations with the court and nobility

outcomes.text: Assess Richelieu's authority and relations with Louis XIII, Gaston d'Orléans, Marie de' Medici and Marillac, including the Day of Dupes.
Explain his statesmanship, raison d'état, edicts and methods.
Explain his policies on the nobility and court: the duelling edict, Montmorency-Bouteville, Cinq Mars, patronage and clientage.
Explain causes: Richelieu's legacy, a royal minority, xenophobia, Mazarin's financial edicts, intendants and relations with nobles, parlements and religious groups.
Describe defeat at Lens and the nature of the Fronde of parlement, nobility and religion, with leaders Condé and Retz.
Explain Mazarin's response, anarchy, Louis XIV, Mazarin's exile, the Peace of Rueil and the Fronde's significance.
Describe Versailles's cultural impact: entertainment, music, ballet, art, architecture, gardens and the Sun King image.
Explain Versailles's political significance: court, mistresses, control of nobility through ritual and etiquette, economic impact and absolutism.
Assess its international significance and reactions.

units.title: Y314 The Challenge of German Nationalism 1789–1919

topics.title: Thematic Study: The Challenge of German Nationalism 1789–1919

outcomes.text: Explain the origins and growth of German nationalism from 1789 and the impact of Napoleon and the Congress of Vienna.
Compare Kleindeutsch and Grossdeutsch views and assess the 1848–1849 revolutions and Frankfurt Parliament.
Explain mass nationalism, the Kulturkampf, Pan-Germanism, radical nationalism and the impact of the First World War and defeat.
Explain economic nationalism and modernisation, the Zollverein and economic integration.
Explain the effects of industrialisation, the rise of socialism, railways, free trade versus protection and their effect on nationalism.
Compare the contributions of Napoleon, Metternich, Bismarck and Wilhelm II in managing nationalism and its opponents.
Explain external forces including Austria's decline, warfare in uniting Germany, the Treaty of Versailles and challenges from left and right.
Assess how far Germany became a united nation, with continuing cultural, religious and regional differences.
Evaluate wars as unifying or divisive, Prussia's role, constitutional developments and the treatment of minorities.
Assess the contribution of liberals, conservatives, socialists and communists, and Prussian domination.
Explain the social, intellectual and economic forces behind the revolutions.
Assess the Frankfurt Parliament's consequences and the revolutions' impact on nationalism.
Explain Metternich's and the authorities' response and support for and opposition to the revolutions.
Assess Bismarck's contribution, use of popular feeling and external forces.
Explain how far the war with France unified people, continuing differences and reasons for Prussian victory.
Evaluate consequences and constitutional developments and Bismarck's statesmanship versus contextual factors 1862–1871.
Describe Wilhelm II's character and ideas and the end of Bismarck's chancellorship's significance for foreign policy.
Explain foreign policy aims and methods and Wilhelm II's relationship with the Reichstag.
Assess military growth, the navy, the army's role, economic growth and the Kaiser's responsibility for the First World War.

units.title: Y315 The Changing Nature of Warfare 1792–1945

topics.title: Thematic Study: The Changing Nature of Warfare 1792–1945

subtopics.title: Factors directly related to the conduct of war

outcomes.text: Assess generalship and the quality of soldiers, including professional armies and volunteers.
Explain the development of strategy, the aims of campaigns, tactics, shock tactics, cult of the offensive and military theorists.
Explain Total War, the involvement of civilians and casualties.
Explain how industrialisation and technology affected war, including telegraph, radio, telephone, radar, steamboats, railways and the internal combustion engine.
Describe developments in weaponry: the rifle, artillery, machine gun, tanks and aeroplane.
Assess the effectiveness of alliances and military plans.
Describe developments in organisation, command and control of armies.
Explain the organisation of the state for war: recruitment, supplies, scale and government intervention.
Explain public opinion, morale, patriotism, mass literacy, franchise, the popular press, censorship and conscription.
Explain the economics and cost of war, mobilisation of the economy, mass production, manpower and resources.

topics.title: Depth Studies: The Changing Nature of Warfare

outcomes.text: Assess generalship, soldier quality, and the development of tactics and strategy.
Explain developments in communication, weaponry, alliances and army organisation.
Explain conscription, manpower and resources.
Assess generalship, soldier quality, and the development of tactics and strategy.
Explain industrialisation, communication and transport, and weaponry.
Explain alliances, army organisation, public opinion, conscription, manpower and resources.

subtopics.title: The Western Front and the First World War 1914–1918

outcomes.text: Assess generalship, soldier quality, tactics, strategy and military theorists.
Explain Total War, communication, industrialisation, transport and weaponry.
Explain alliances, army organisation, the state's organisation for war, public opinion, conscription, manpower and resources.

units.title: Y316 Britain and Ireland 1791–1921

outcomes.text: Describe revolutionary nationalism: Wolfe Tone and United Irishmen, Young Ireland, the Fenians, Land League, Sinn Féin, Easter Rising and Anglo-Irish War.
Describe constitutional nationalism: O'Connell, Parnell and Redmond, Catholic Emancipation and Home Rule.
Explain cultural nationalism 1798–1921 and the role of the Catholic Church in opposition.
Explain the Protestant Ascendancy and its decline from the 1870s.
Explain Unionism, Ulster Unionism 1886–1921 and its strategies.
Describe the policies of the Conservative, Whig and Liberal parties and the role of the Anglican and Presbyterian Churches.
Explain the creation of the Act of Union and reform within the Union from 1829.
Describe reforms in administration, education, land and local government, Home Rule and Partition.

subtopics.title: The Irish economy and Irish Nationalism

outcomes.text: Explain agrarian under-development, population pressures, land and economic issues in relation to nationalism.
Explain the impact of the Famine 1845–1849, industrialisation and Ulster, and North/South differences.
Explain Irish politics in the late 18th century and the impact of the French Revolution: Catholic Committee, United Irishmen, Orange Order and Bantry Bay.
Describe the British response (Fitzwilliam, Lake, Castlereagh) and the 1798 Wolfe Tone Rising: causes, leadership, support and consequences.
Explain Grattan's Parliament, Pitt and the Act of Union 1800.
Explain Emmet's Rising of 1803 and the impact of the rebellions on revolutionary nationalism.
Explain the Catholic Association's strategies, government response and O'Connell's leadership to 1829.
Describe the Waterford and Clare elections and the Brunswick Clubs.
Explain Catholic Emancipation's reasons and impact to 1841: O'Connell and the Whigs, the Tithe War, the Irish Church, Lichfield House compact.
Explain Redmond, Home Rule and Asquith's Liberal government, the 1912 Home Rule Bill and negotiations over exclusion.
Explain Ulster Unionist reasons and tactics: Carson, Craig, Bonar Law, the Solemn League and Covenant and the Ulster Volunteers.
Describe the nationalist Irish Volunteers, government response (Curragh Mutiny), the situation in 1914 and enactment and suspension of Home Rule.

units.title: Y317 China and its Rulers 1839–1989

topics.title: Thematic Study: China and its Rulers 1839–1989

subtopics.title: The government and rulers of China 1839–1989

outcomes.text: Describe Manchu rule in 1839, rebellions and obstacles to reform under Cixi, and reforms after 1900.
Explain the 1911 Revolution, Sun Yat Sen and the new Republic, and the rule of Yuan Shikai.
Describe the Guomindang and Jiang Jieshi, the Communist takeover, Mao's government, changes after 1975 and Deng Xiaoping.
Describe the Chinese economy in 1839 and Manchu developments: railways, trade, industry and agrarian problems.
Describe industrial and urban development under the Guomindang and land reform under Communism.
Explain the Four Year Plans, the Great Leap Forward, Mao's later economic policy and economic change after Mao with regional variations.
Describe society under Manchu rule: Confucianism, women, rural society and later Manchu changes including the Boxers.
Explain social developments after 1911, social factors in the rise of Communism and social change after 1949.
Explain the Cultural Revolution's effect on society, development after 1975 and the rise of the middle class.
Explain foreign influence in Manchu China: the Opium Wars, the sack of Beijing, Unequal Treaties and reaction to the Boxer Rebellion.
Describe Japanese aggression 1898–1945, Jiang Jieshi's relations with the USSR and USA, and the Korean War.
Explain relations with the West after 1949 and China as a regional power in South Asia.

topics.title: Depth Studies: China and its Rulers

subtopics.title: The First Opium War and its impact

outcomes.text: Explain China and the Western powers by 1839 and the long- and short-term causes of the war, including the opium trade.
Describe Commissioner Lin's influence, British reaction and the outbreak and nature of the war.
Explain the Ch'uan-pi Convention, Treaty of Nanjing, Treaty of the Bogue, and the results including the Unequal Treaties.
Explain resentment of foreign influence, the 1898 coup, economic hardship and the origin of the Boxers and their links to the Court.
Describe attacks on foreign legations, the refusal of Southeast China to join, foreign forces and the defeat of the uprising.
Explain the consequences: the 1901 Boxer protocol, Russian expansion, Open Door policy, China's reputation and the weakening of the dynasty.
Explain the origins and causes, problems by 1966, the Great Leap Forward's failure, and Mao's concerns about Liu Shao-chi.
Explain the influence of Lin Biao, Chen Boda, Jiang Qing and the Gang of Four, Politburo changes and the army.
Describe the course of the Cultural Revolution, Red Guards, decline of violence, demobilisation and Lin Biao's death, and its economic, political and social effects.

units.title: Y318 Russia and its Rulers 1855–1964

topics.title: Thematic Study: Russia and its Rulers 1855–1964

outcomes.text: Explain autocracy, dictatorship and totalitarianism and developments in central administration.
Describe methods of repression and enforcement, the extent and impact of reform and changes in local government.
Assess opposition before and after 1917 and the attitudes of Tsars, Provisional Government and Communists to political change.

subtopics.title: Impact of dictatorial regimes on the economy and society

outcomes.text: Explain changes to urban and rural living and working conditions: Emancipation, Land Banks, famines, NEP, collectivisation and Virgin Lands.
Explain the impact of industrial growth under the Tsars, War Communism, NEP and the Five Year Plans on workers.
Describe limits on personal, political and religious freedom and the extent of economic and social change.
Explain the effects on government, society, nationalities and economy of the Crimean War and Japanese War.
Explain the effects of the 1905 and 1917 Revolutions, both World Wars and the Cold War.
Describe the Polish Revolt 1863, expansion in Asia, Russification, Finland and the Baltic provinces.
Explain the impact of the First World War and Brest Litovsk, the Russo-Polish War and Communist advance into Eastern and Central Europe after 1945.

topics.title: Depth Studies: Russia and its Rulers

outcomes.text: Explain the effects of the Crimean War and the aims of Alexander II's domestic policies.
Describe the nature of his government, changes in central administration and the extent and impact of reform.
Assess opposition, changes in living and working conditions, limits on freedom and the extent of change.
Describe the Provisional Government's main domestic policies and nature, and its methods of repression.
Assess reform, opposition, living and working conditions, freedom and social change.
Explain the impact of the continuing war and the reasons for the Provisional Government's overthrow.
Describe Khrushchev's aims, government, opposition and repression in Russia and satellites.
Assess reform, living and working conditions, freedom, economic planning and the Virgin Lands Scheme.
Explain the impact of the Cold War and Khrushchev's fall.

units.title: Y319 Civil Rights in the USA 1865–1992

topics.title: Thematic Study: Civil Rights in the USA 1865–1992

outcomes.text: Describe African Americans' position in 1865, Reconstruction, white reaction and discrimination.
Assess the roles of Booker T Washington, Du Bois, Martin Luther King and the Black Panthers.
Explain the roles of Federal and State governments, anti- and pro-civil rights groups, and the Civil Rights Movement to 1992.
Describe union and labour rights in 1865 and the impact of New Immigration and industrialisation.
Explain the role of Federal governments and the impact of the World Wars.
Assess the significance of the 1960s, Chavez and the UFW, and the Reagan era.
Describe the position of Native Americans in 1865 and the impact of the Plains Wars.
Explain the impact of the Dawes Act, citizenship in 1924, the New Deal and the American Indian Movement.
Describe Native Americans and the Supreme Court, and pressure groups.
Describe women's position in 1865 and the impact of the prohibition and suffrage campaigns.
Explain the impact of the New Deal and World Wars.
Explain the rise of feminism and its opponents, Roe v Wade, the Equal Rights Amendment and changing economic opportunities.

topics.title: Depth Studies: Civil Rights in the USA

subtopics.title: Civil rights in the Gilded Age c.1875–c.1895

outcomes.text: Assess the nature and extent of civil rights progress and the varied impact of industrialisation on women, African Americans and workers.
Evaluate government policy and the attitudes of Presidents, Congress, the Supreme Court and States.
Explain the impact of Westward Expansion on civil rights and the north-south and east-west divides.

subtopics.title: The New Deal and civil rights

outcomes.text: Describe the situation of women, African Americans, Native Americans and workers by 1932.
Assess Roosevelt's motives and how far the New Deal improved status and rights for each group.
Evaluate opposition to the New Deal, especially the Second New Deal and workers' rights.
Assess Malcolm X's aims, motivations, methods, success and how they changed.
Explain the rise of Black Power and its impact on other civil rights groups and Non-Violent Direct Action.
Evaluate Black Power's success and its relationship with women's and workers' causes.

units.title: Y320 From Colonialism to Independence: The British Empire 1857–1965

topics.title: Thematic Study: From Colonialism to Independence: The British Empire 1857–1965

subtopics.title: Governance and administration of the Empire

outcomes.text: Describe the Empire in 1857 and explain its growth: formal and informal empire, New Imperialism and the Berlin Conference.
Evaluate economic explanations (overseas investment, crisis of capitalism, gentlemanly capitalism), imperial rivalry and metropolitan influence.
Describe forms of governance, security and coercion, trusteeship, men on the spot, collaboration, technology and negotiation.
Explain peaceful and violent opposition movements in South Africa, India, Sudan, Malaya and Kenya.
Explain the rise of nationalism: India and Gandhi, Kenya and Kenyatta, Nkrumah and Pan-Africanism, with methods, success and consequences.

subtopics.title: Impact of imperial power on periphery and Britain

outcomes.text: Describe impact on colonies: Orientalism, work, famine, technology, disease and medicine, identities, religion, gender, education and indigenous culture.
Describe impact on Britain: jingoism, exhibitions, school texts, youth organisations, the arts, politics, international relations and the economy.
Explain Empire and European rivalry, Splendid Isolation and its end, colonial wars and the World Wars.
Describe Empire and relations with the League of Nations, UN, USA, the Cold War, the Commonwealth, Europe and the EEC.

subtopics.title: British India: The War of 1857 and its consequences to 1876

outcomes.text: Describe British India in 1857, the course of the rebellion and why it failed.
Explain consequences in India and internationally, including British attitudes and methods of rule.
Explain the Zionist-Palestinian problem by 1914, the First World War and the Balfour Declaration.
Describe the British Mandate, interwar uprisings, immigration and their consequences.
Explain the reasons for and immediate consequences of partition in 1948.
Explain reasons for the rise of nationalism and the Mau Mau rebellion: causes, nature and impact.
Describe the problem of settlers and the Indian population, and Kenyatta's importance.
Explain changing British policy under Macmillan, the independence settlement and the international context.

units.title: Y321 The Middle East 1908–2011: Ottomans to Arab Spring

topics.title: Thematic Study: The Middle East 1908–2011: Ottomans to Arab Spring

outcomes.text: Explain the aims, policies and methods of Britain and France to 1956 and Russia and the US to 2011.
Describe the League of Nations and UN, mandates, coups, occupations, bases and client states, and Great Power war involvement to the Gulf Wars.
Explain Great Powers and resources: oil, the Seven Sisters, nationalisation, the Mossadeq coup, OPEC and oil as a weapon.

subtopics.title: Zionism, Israel and the Palestinian issue

outcomes.text: Explain Zionist ideas, the impact of the World Wars, the Jewish Agency and the creation of Israel and the 1948 War.
Describe the Arab-Israeli Wars, invasions of Lebanon and Gaza, the Occupied Territories, settlements and the Wall.
Explain Israeli diplomacy including Sadat, Camp David, Oslo and the Road Map.
Explain Palestinian refugees, the PLO and Arafat, the Intifadas, Palestinian divisions and the Palestinian Authority and conflict over resources.
Explain the progress of Arabism from 1908, Nasser and the Arab revolution in Egypt and Syria and the United Arab Republic.
Describe the impact of Arab-Israeli Wars and regional rivalries.
Compare democratic, monarchical and authoritarian states: Ataturk's Turkey, Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Wahhabism.
Describe Syria, the Baathists and Assads, Iraq from Faisal to Saddam and the US, and Iran from the Shah to the Ayatollahs.
Explain Sunni and Shi'a in the Arab States, Egypt and the Muslim Brotherhood, and the Iranian Islamic Revolution.
Describe Hezbollah, Hamas, Al Qaeda and Christian communities including Lebanon, Armenians and Copts.
Describe Jewish communities, ethnic minorities including Kurds, and the role of the Middle Eastern diaspora.

subtopics.title: British Policy and the Middle East 1908–1948

outcomes.text: Explain British imperial aims before 1914 and the wartime partition: Sykes-Picot, the Balfour Declaration, McMahon-Hussein letters and peace treaties.
Describe the Mandates of Palestine and Transjordan, British oil companies and relations with Faisal and Iraq.
Explain relations with Arabs and Jews, British Egypt, the Second World War, the Biltmore Declaration and withdrawal from Palestine in 1948.
Describe Arab attitudes in 1948 towards Palestinians and the creation of Israel.
Explain the First Arab-Israeli War 1948–1949 and Israel's survival.
Explain the Suez Crisis and Second Arab-Israeli War, Israel's success, and the impact on Palestinians and the Arab world.
Explain Nasser and Pan Arabism and Arab Socialism: nationalisation, land reform and development from above.
Describe relations with Britain, France, the US and USSR and the Suez Crisis.
Explain the Arab Cold War, the United Arab Republic, Non-Alignment, the 1967 War and the death of Pan Arabism.
